chapters.title: Notification settings and e-mail templates
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how agents are notified by default: in the app, by e-mail, by push or in a digest.
It also shows how to change the wording of the automatic e-mails that SupportDesk sends to customers and agents.

sections.title: The delivery defaults page
intro: To open it, select **Administration** > **Notifications & e-mail templates**. The **Delivery defaults** tab opens first.
You need the **Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars** or the **Manage email accounts and messaging channels** permission.

blocks.caption: The **Delivery defaults** tab with the channel for each event.
blocks.alt: Delivery defaults tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the information note, the column headings, the first event row, the quiet hours card and the save bar

callouts: A reminder of how the rules work together.
The four delivery channels. The box in each heading ticks or clears the whole column.
One row per event. Tick the channels that agents get by default.
**Quiet hours & digests**: when e-mail and push wait, and when digests go out.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Save defaults**.

rows: A notification under the bell icon in the desk.
An e-mail right away, or after quiet hours end.
A notification on the mobile app.
The event is bundled into the hourly or daily digest e-mail.

blocks.note: When both **E-mail** and **Digest** are ticked, the event goes into the digest. It does not come as a separate e-mail.

sections.title: Notification events
sections.intro: These are the events on the **Delivery defaults** tab.

rows: A ticket is assigned to the agent.
Someone mentions the agent with @ in a ticket.
A customer replies on a ticket the agent owns or watches.
A ticket the agent is involved in is escalated.
An SLA target is about to be missed.
The agent is asked to approve something.
A request the agent raised was approved or rejected.
The AI proposes an action that needs a decision.
Unusual ticket volume or sentiment is found.
A visitor is waiting in live chat.
A live chat is transferred to the agent or to their department.

sections.title: Set the default channels per event
sections.intro: Decide how agents hear about each event, unless they choose otherwise.
prerequisites: You have the **Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars** or **Manage email accounts and messaging channels** permission.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Notifications & e-mail templates**.
On the **Delivery defaults** tab, tick or clear the boxes for each event.
To change a whole column, tick or clear the box in its heading.
Select **Save defaults**.
sections.result: The app shows **Notification defaults saved**. The save bar shows **All changes saved** and the version number.
blocks: To undo your changes before you save, select **Discard**.

blocks.note: The page says agents can override these defaults. In this release, the desk has no page for agents to do that yet.

sections.title: Set quiet hours and digests
sections.intro: Quiet hours hold back e-mail and push notifications at night. Digests bundle notifications into one e-mail.
steps: On the **Delivery defaults** tab, find the **Quiet hours & digests** card.
Turn on **Quiet hours**.

steps.text: Enter the times in **From** and **Until**, such as `22:00` and `07:00`.
steps.caption: Quiet hours switched on, with the time zone and the digest settings.
steps.alt: Quiet hours and digests card with Quiet hours on, From, Until, Time zone, Digest frequency and Daily digest at

steps: Choose the **Time zone**.
Choose the **Digest frequency**: **Hourly** or **Daily**.
For a daily digest, enter the time in **Daily digest at**. The default is `08:00`.
Select **Save defaults**.
sections.result: E-mail and push notifications wait until quiet hours end. In-app notifications still appear at once.

blocks.note: Critical alerts ignore quiet hours. Quiet hours must end at a different time than they start.

sections.title: E-mail templates
intro: SupportDesk sends four automatic e-mails. Each one has a built-in wording that you can replace with your own.
Select the **E-mail templates** tab to see them.

blocks.caption: The **E-mail templates** tab, grouped by who receives the e-mail.
blocks.alt: E-mail templates tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the To customers heading, a template name with its badge, its subject line and Edit

callouts: The template name and its badge.
The current subject line, and when someone last changed it.

rows: A customer's e-mail creates a ticket, and the mailbox sends acknowledgements.
A ticket is resolved, and satisfaction surveys are on.
An agent gets an e-mail for a notification, such as an assignment or a mention.
The hourly or daily digest goes out.
You saved your own wording but switched it off, so the built-in wording is used.

sections.title: Customise an e-mail template
sections.intro: Change the subject and text of an automatic e-mail. The preview shows the result with sample values.
steps: On the **E-mail templates** tab, select **Edit** on a template.
Change the **Subject**.
Change the **Body (HTML)**.
To add a value such as the ticket number, place the cursor and select a placeholder chip next to **Insert:**.
Turn on **Use this custom template (off = built-in default)**.
Check the **Preview**. For customer e-mails, choose a brand to see its footer.
Select **Save template**.
sections.result: The app shows **Template saved**. The template's badge changes to **Customised**.

blocks.caption: The editor of the **New ticket acknowledgement** template.
blocks.alt: Template editor with numbered highlights on the title and badges, Subject, Body (HTML), the placeholder chips, the custom template switch, the preview and the save bar

callouts: The template name, who receives it and its badge.
**Subject**: the subject line, up to 500 characters.
The placeholder chips. Point to a chip to see what it means.
The switch that turns your wording on or off.
**Preview**: the e-mail with sample values and the brand's footer.
The save bar with **Reset to default**, **Discard** and **Save template**.

blocks.note: SupportDesk removes unsafe code from the e-mail. It inserts values as plain text.

blocks.warning: There is no test send. Check the **Preview** carefully before you save.

sections.title: E-mail template placeholders
sections.intro: A placeholder is a word in double braces. SupportDesk replaces it with the real value when it sends the e-mail. Only the placeholders of each template are allowed.

rows: `{{contact.name}}` customer's name, `{{brand.name}}` brand or mailbox name, `{{ticket.number}}` ticket reference, `{{ticket.subject}}` ticket subject, `{{portal.url}}` help center address.

`{{ticket.number}}`, `{{ticket.subject}}`, `{{agent.name}}` agent who resolved the ticket, `{{survey.link}}` survey address, `{{survey.buttons}}` rating buttons 1 to 5, `{{survey.expires}}` expiry date, `{{brand.name}}`.
`{{user.name}}` agent's name, `{{notification.title}}`, `{{notification.body}}` notification text, `{{notification.link}}` link to the record.
`{{user.name}}`, `{{digest.count}}` number of items, `{{digest.items}}` list of notifications.

blocks.note: If you type a placeholder that the template does not know, the preview warns you. The app does not save the template until you fix it.

sections.title: Go back to the built-in wording
sections.intro: You can switch your wording off for a while, or delete it.
steps: Open the template on the **E-mail templates** tab.
To pause your wording, turn off **Use this custom template (off = built-in default)**. Then select **Save template**.
To delete your wording, select **Reset to default**.
In the confirmation, select **Reset**.
sections.result: The app shows **Template reset to the default**. The badge changes to **Default**.

blocks.warning: **Reset to default** deletes your subject and body. You cannot get them back.

sections.title: How the satisfaction survey e-mail works
sections.intro: The survey e-mail asks the customer to rate the help they got.

list: The rating buttons open the feedback page of the brand's help center, with the chosen star selected.
The customer confirms the rating and can add a comment.
The customer does not need to sign in. The link itself proves who they are, and it expires.
Signed-in customers can also rate a ticket from its page in the help center.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the template has unknown placeholders.
troubleshooting.cause: The subject or body contains a placeholder that this template does not support.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove it, or insert one of the chips shown next to **Insert:**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app asks for a subject or a body.
troubleshooting.cause: The **Subject** or **Body (HTML)** is empty or too long.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a subject of up to 500 characters and a body.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says to set both the start and the end of quiet hours.
troubleshooting.cause: Only one of **From** and **Until** has a time.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter both times, or turn off **Quiet hours**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says quiet hours must end at a different time.
A **Discard unsaved changes?** message appears when you leave the page.
troubleshooting.cause: You changed something and did not save it.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Keep editing** and save. Or select **Discard changes** to leave without saving.

troubleshooting.problem: Agents get no notification e-mails at night.
troubleshooting.cause: Quiet hours are on. E-mail and push wait until they end.
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected. Critical alerts still go out.

faq.q: Can I send a test e-mail from a template?
faq.a: No. Use the **Preview**, which fills in sample values and adds the brand's footer.

faq.q: Can each brand have its own template?
faq.a: No. Each template is shared by all brands. Use `{{brand.name}}` for the brand name. SupportDesk adds each brand's e-mail footer to customer e-mails.

faq.q: Why do agents get a digest instead of separate e-mails?
faq.a: For events where both **E-mail** and **Digest** are ticked, SupportDesk bundles the event into the digest.

glossary.definition: The administrator's choice of how agents are notified of each event: in the app, by e-mail, by push or in a digest.
One e-mail that bundles several notifications, sent every hour or once a day.
Hours when SupportDesk holds back e-mail and push notifications. Critical alerts still go out.
The subject and text of an automatic e-mail that SupportDesk sends.
A word in double braces, such as `{{ticket.number}}`, that SupportDesk replaces with a real value.
